Messengers of Allah (Risalah) Muslims are often named after prophets.
Day of Judgement Muslims are affected by this belief to make sure they live as Allah has guided them to, so that they will be judged well.
Decree of Allah Muslims believe they should try to accept God’s will – what God wants for them and the whole universe.

ideas: To start Hajj, pilgrims circle the Ka’bah seven times counter-clockwise at the Great Mosque in Makkah.
The pilgrims then move on to Mina, four miles to the east of Makkah, where they camp.
At the end of the day, Muslims walk to Muzdalifah and collect pebbles.
On the morning of the third day, pilgrims walk to Mina and throw pebbles at stone pillars that stand for Satan.

At the end of the third day, Muslims walk back to Makkah. They sacrifice animals to remember when Ibrahim (Abraham) had shown his faith in Allah by offering to sacrifice his son Isma’il, but Allah replaced it with a ram.

q.a: Outline three Muslim beliefs about the creation of the universe.
q.b: Explain two reasons Muslims accept the universe as valuable.

q.d: “The Big Bang shows that Allah did not create the universe.”

ideas: This theory says that the universe started around 13.7 billion years ago when a single, incredibly hot point started to cool and expand (grow).
Everything in the universe is within this expanding dot – the Big Bang continues to this day.
Matter (physical stuff) grouped together in places and this is how galaxies and stars were formed.

After old stars exploded they left more complicated kinds of matter (beyond just hydrogen and helium) and this was caught up in the gravity of new stars, and is what planets like Earth, and everything on them – including us – are made of.
There is a particular kind of background radiation that the theory said would be everywhere and that was discovered after the theory had been put forward.

Astronomers have seen that all the galaxies are moving away from each other. If we were to ‘re-wind’ this would mean everything would move back together – to the small point which the Big Bang said was there at the start of the universe.
Scientific-minded Muslims think science and the Qur’an are compatible (can both be true at the same time)

They see a ‘day’ as a poetic way of talking about a long time in the creation verses of the Qur’an, so the Qur’an and scientific theories can agree about the universe being many billions of years old.

There are verses in the Qur’an that seem to match the Big Bang. For example, it says: ‘the heavens and the earth used to be joined together and We (Allah and the malaikah/angels) ripped them apart.’ (Surah 21:30).
Muslims would argue that if everything has a cause, then the Big Bang needs a cause too.
There is a long history of science and mathematics in Islam, which is celebrated by Muslims today.
If the universe was created by the Big Bang, then there is no need to use Allah as an explanation.
There is no scientific evidence for Allah, but there is for the Big Bang.
Muslims believe that Allah made the universe for humans as a commodity. People are the most important part of the universe.

ideas: There are many passages in the Qur’an that teach that there is a Day of Judgement and akhirah (life after death).
